definitions.explanation: The state or process of becoming accustomed to something through experience.
A negative sense where excessive familiarity leads to carelessness or taking things for granted.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}は{慣|な}れが{大事|だいじ}だ。
examples.english: Getting used to the work is important.

examples.japanese: {運転|うんてん}は{慣|な}れの{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: Driving is a matter of getting used to it.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{環境|かんきょう}にも{慣|な}れてきて、{毎日|まいにち}が{楽|たの}しくなった。
examples.english: I've gotten used to the new environment, and every day has become enjoyable.

examples.japanese: {慣|な}れから{油断|ゆだん}が{生|う}まれる。
{長年|ながねん}の{慣|な}れで{安全|あんぜん}{確認|かくにん}を{怠|おこた}ってしまった。
examples.english: Due to years of complacency, I neglected the safety check.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {慣|な}れる (to get accustomed to). Has both a positive sense (gaining experience) and a negative sense (becoming complacent).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣|な}れの{問題|もんだい} — a matter of getting used to it
- {慣|な}れが{必要|ひつよう} — requires getting accustomed
- {慣|な}れからくる{油断|ゆだん} — carelessness from over-familiarity
- {慣|な}れは{怖|こわ}い — complacency is dangerous

USAGE:
Sense 1 is encouraging — emphasizing that practice and exposure will make things easier. Sense 2 is cautionary — warning that too much familiarity leads to mistakes. The phrase {慣|な}れは{怖|こわ}い is a common warning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {経験|けいけん} — experience (broader, emphasizes what was learned)
- {習慣|しゅうかん} — habit (repeated behavior, not the process of adapting)
